messages.author: 56504f6cee0a1bab
messages.subject: no audio drivers are available ?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to deploy an app on shinyapps.io but I run into a problem to do with the audiodriver.
The app loads a .wav file and plays it through the 'play()' function of package audio. I choose this approach over the js approach as I want reactive control to pause/rewind/resume (if that's also possible with the JS approach then I'd be happy to take that as an alternative solution).

Yet, when deploying the app on shinyapps.io I run into the following error:

Error in value[[3L]](cond) : no audio drivers are available Calls: local ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous> Execution halted

from the info here (http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/appendix.html#default-system-packages)I deduce that an audio driver is available but I can't quite figure out how to make the app connect/use it?

Any great ideas would be super welcome!

All best,

Anne

messages.author: 299a5089d6c6c523
messages.subject: Re: no audio drivers are available ?
parts:
My read of the audio package is that on Unix/Linux, there is experimental support for portaudio.
The system package that would need to be installed is likely https://packages.ubuntu.com/trusty/libportaudio-dev

However, even if there were an audio driver, the sound would be played back on the server, not on the user's computer, which is why you likely want a browser based playback mechanism.

Hi Joshua,

Thanks!  I was sort of afraid that the server playing thing may apply here too.

However, it certainly is possible to play sound in/through the browser in a shinyapps.io hosted app using
 
       tags$audio(src = "zaksinter.wav", type = "audio/wav", autoplay = T, controls = T),

which even adds a nice audio control (if set) etc.  I guess I'll try to figure out a way to reactively control javascript instead of relying on package audio's play().
If it at all possible I'd like to get this to work in the next couple of hours, so any advice is welcome :)  I'd like to reactively control when playback starts and that the wav either loops automatically or is reactively restarted.. :)

All best,

Anne

messages.author: 56504f6cee0a1bab
messages.subject: Re: no audio drivers are available ?
parts:
So... that turned out to be much simpler than I thought.

The audio$tag can be generated through renderUI. So...

in the UI:

     uiOutput("audiotag"),

in the server:

       output$audiotag<-renderUI(tags$audio( src = "zaksinter.wav",
                                            type ="audio/wav", autoplay = T, controls = T, loop="loop"))
     
 
The .wav file needs to be uploaded inside a www folder and then it all works beautifully : )
